151: #: a free-text note about this claim's *standing* or its *attribution*;
152: #: ``None`` when there is nothing to record.  It carries **two distinct
153: #: meanings** (U5.19 added the second), so -- stated plainly -- since U5.19
154: #: a non-``None`` value does **not** imply that this claim was downgraded:
155: #:
156: #: 1. **cap reason** -- a *declared* standing was capped below ``CONFIRMS`` ...
160: #: 2. **provenance-divergence note** (U5.19, F2) -- ``producer`` names the
161: #:    *assessing* authority ... 163: #:    legitimately remain ``CONFIRMS``.
166: #: The two are **not mutually exclusive**: each writer *appends* ...
169: #: it caps), so one field can carry both statements ``"; "``-joined.  A
170: #: consumer must therefore not read ``verdict_reason is not None`` as "this
171: #: claim was downgraded" -- the authoritative downgrade signal is ``verdict``.
172: #: ... Nor is the value structured: a clause may itself contain ``"; "`` ...
175: #: clauses.  What *is* reliable is substring detection of the known
176: #: writers: ``"capped at EXTENDS"`` is emitted by every cap site and by
177: #: nothing else, and ``"is the *assessing* producer"`` by the divergence
178: #: site alone.

Nothing in the docstring (or previously in the repo) pinned either string, so the guarantee was unfalsifiable prose: 'reliable' is safe only relative to the current writers and only once the handed-up guard lands. A consumer must treat it as a hint, not a contract; the real fix is the typed assessed_by/mined_by field U5.23 handed up.
